stem:
For a school science project, Priya wants to make a simple Voltaic cell at home. She knows that a working cell needs two electrodes made of different metals and an electrolyte to conduct electricity between them. She connects an LED in the circuit to test each setup.
Which of her setups will work as a Voltaic cell?

options.text: Two copper wires pushed into a lemon, connected to the LED
A copper strip and an iron nail pushed into a lemon, connected to the LED
A copper strip and an iron nail placed in a glass of distilled water, connected to the LED
Two iron nails pushed into a potato, connected to the LED

teacher.key_rationale: A working Voltaic cell requires two different metal electrodes and an electrolyte. B has copper and iron (different metals) in a lemon, whose citric acid juice acts as an electrolyte, so the LED glows. A and D use two electrodes of the same metal, and C lacks an electrolyte (distilled water does not conduct), so none of these produce a current.
